espn-603999.headline: Three fly-halves down, France hand Dupont the 10
beats: Romain Ntamack hurt his shoulder against Fiji, joining Matthieu Jalibert and Antoine Hastoy on the injury list, with Thomas Ramos out too. So Antoine Dupont, captain and scrum-half, starts a Test at fly-half for the first time, opposite Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu.

The Stade de France is not gentle ground for an experiment. South Africa won here 32–17 last November and have taken the last five meetings in Paris, dating back to 2013. France last beat them in the city in 2005.

Julien Marchand comes in at hooker to shore up a set-piece that may take a beating, and François Cros says France must match South Africa physically before they can think about playing. Manage that and win, and France go third in the world while South Africa drop to second, behind New Zealand.
Maxime Lucu played at 10 when Ntamack went off against Fiji. Now he is at scrum-half, feeding the man who usually feeds the 10.

espn-604000.headline: Argentina need a hooker, and Benetton have one
beats: Julián Montoya, 121 caps, is out for 12 days on HIA protocols after leaving early in Dublin. Leonel Oviedo, who replaced him, was also assessed, and Ignacio Ruiz is injured. So Argentina called up Bautista Bernasconi of Benetton, three caps, and Facundo Bosch, 35, who last played for them in 2021.

Italy have lost five straight and conceded 66, 57 and 47 in their last three. Their hooker, Tommaso Di Bartolomeo, says the plan is to put pressure on the scrum and the lineout. That is exactly where a borrowed hooker would feel it.
The shortage runs to the back. Juan Cruz Mallía sprained a knee against Ireland, and Santiago Carreras is out for the year.
Win, and Italy go up to 9th in the world, above Fiji and Wales. Fiji are their next visitors.

espn-604001.headline: Thirty-four defeats, and seats now going for £20
beats: Wales have lost all 34 matches against New Zealand since 1953. Days before the 35th, the union cut student tickets in Cardiff from £98 to £20, having recently posted annual losses of £18 million.

Last November Wales lost 26–52 at home. New Zealand have scored seven tries in each of their last three games, including 43–21 at Murrayfield last week. They are level on points with South Africa but second in their conference.

Dave Rennie is set to make wholesale changes, with Will Jordan in doubt, though he says "We will still put out a damn good side". Wales are sweating on Aaron Wainwright at number eight. A win would lift them to 9th in the world, above Fiji.
Jonathan Davies wants Wales to think like FA Cup giant-killers. They are priced as long as 33/1. The students got the better deal.

espn-604002.headline: Jones gave Alex Coles his first cap. Now he must stop him
beats: Eddie Jones spent seven divisive years as England coach. He brings Japan, ranked 12th, to Allianz Stadium to face a side ranked 5th, and Alex Coles, the lock he gave a debut, says he will always be grateful. Gratitude tends to stop at kick-off.

Jones is candid about the gap: "if we play an orthodox game of rugby, we’re probably going to struggle to beat them." Japan lost 21–28 to Wales in Cardiff last week, close enough for a bonus point and not much else.

England put seven tries past Australia in a 45–22 win and paid for it. Seb Atkinson's hip and Immanuel Feyi-Waboso's ankle, which ends his November, leave the No.12 and left-wing shirts open, with Max Ojomoh tipped for midfield.
Only a Japan win by 16 or more drops England to sixth, below Scotland. New Zealand arrive a week later, so England need more than a win here. They need their midfield answer to work.

espn-604003.headline: Fiji have no points, and Ireland still want rain
beats: Fiji have lost all four Nations Championship games, the last 54-17 to France in Paris. Stuart McCloskey still expects a physical evening, and his plan includes the forecast: "hopefully there's a bit of rain so they don't offload as much."

Ireland scored six tries in beating Argentina 42-12, but come in short. Captain Dan Sheehan is out of this game, and Sean Jansen's knee has ended his campaign, thinning the options at number eight. Andy Farrell may rotate as well.
That is where the risk sits. Ireland have been third in the world all season, and a Fiji win would drop them to fifth, below France and England.
Fiji then go to Italy, the only other side without a point. Ireland host South Africa, who have won all four, and rain will not do much for them there.

espn-604004.headline: The 21–43 club meets at Murrayfield
beats: Scotland lost 21–43 to New Zealand at Murrayfield on 7 November. Australia lost to New Zealand by exactly that score in October, a week after conceding 50 to them.

Australia then shipped 45 to England at Twickenham, their third straight defeat. Planet Rugby's Hamish Bidwell called that "a second-rate game played by second-rate combatants" and reckons Scotland are "more at their level".
That level is close. Scotland are sixth in the world and Australia seventh, and an Australian win would swap them.
Both have spent the autumn on the wrong end of 43. On Sunday one of them gets to be on the other end of something.

espn-604005.headline: England's new forward was a Māori All Black in 2022
beats: Max Hicks was born in Auckland and played Super Rugby for the Highlanders. He qualifies through his Cornish mother. The 27-year-old Newcastle forward is one of six England call-ups, and he could make his Test debut against New Zealand.
New Zealand's soft spot is in the forwards. Assistant coach Neil Barnes admits they must fix their maul defence after Scotland found them out, even in a 43–21 win at Murrayfield.
England won the last meeting, 33–19 at home on 15 November 2025. New Zealand are unbeaten in this competition, and a win by 16 or more takes them above South Africa to first in the world.
Four years after representing the Māori All Blacks, Hicks may be part of the reason they stay second.

espn-604006.headline: Scotland have a maul. Japan want a mess.
beats: Scotland lost 21–43 to New Zealand at Murrayfield on 7 November and still came away with a weapon. Two of their tries came from the driving maul, Ewan Ashman finished with a hat-trick, and the All Blacks' coaches have spent the week explaining their maul defence.

Japan come to Edinburgh after Twickenham, where Eddie Jones's stated plan is to "break up the game" because an orthodox one would not suit them. They lost 21–28 in Cardiff on 7 November, a game they let slip.
Scotland's trouble is the other end. They have let in 43 twice this year, to Ireland and to New Zealand. A Japan win by 16 or more would drop Scotland to eighth, below Australia and Argentina.
Japan's whole idea is to make the game untidy. Scotland's best rugby this month came from the tidiest set-piece in the sport.

espn-604007.headline: Ireland's scrum has had a year to think about it
beats: South Africa won 24–13 in Dublin last November in a game of 20 scrums. Ireland conceded six scrum penalties and a penalty try, and Andrew Porter and Paddy McCarthy were both yellow-carded. Porter did not play for Ireland again until Argentina this month.

The scrum held in that 42–12 win, with two penalties won and none conceded. The forwards are thinner now. Sean Jansen's knee has ended his campaign. Dan Sheehan, captaining in place of the injured Caelan Doris, is on a 12-day return-to-play protocol after a concussion.
South Africa arrive unbeaten in the championship and scored nine tries in a 66–7 win in Italy last time out.
An Ireland win would knock South Africa off the top of the world rankings. First place would go to New Zealand, who beat Ireland 40–21 in July.

espn-604008.headline: Bottom two of twelve, playing for ninth in the world
beats: Both arrive in Udine without a Nations Championship point. Between them they are minus 286 on points difference, yet Fiji sit two places above Italy in the world rankings.

Italy have lost five straight and conceded 66 and 57 in their last two. Before this they host Argentina in Genoa, who are without captain Julián Montoya under HIA protocols. Fiji shipped 54 in France but won 34–28 in Japan in October, and they go to Dublin to face Ireland first.
Win by any margin and Italy go up to 9th, above Fiji and Wales. That is a long climb for a side that has won two games all year.
Fiji's next match after this is Spain at home in a World Cup pool, nearly a year away. Whatever happens here, they will have time to think about it.

espn-604009.headline: France are out of fly-halves, not out of tries
beats: With four fly-halves injured, France moved their captain, Antoine Dupont, to 10 for South Africa on 13 November, with Maxime Lucu at nine. Axel Desperes, a 22-year-old fly-half from Pau, was set for his debut against the world champions.
The tries have not dried up yet. France scored eight against Fiji on 7 November and arrive at the Stade de France on three straight wins.

Argentina have gaps of their own. Julián Montoya, 121 caps, went off in the 42–12 defeat to Ireland in Dublin and missed Italy in Genoa under HIA protocols. At fullback, Santiago Carreras is out for the year and Juan Cruz Mallía sprained a knee.

Argentina have one win in 2026. Win here and France slip below England to fifth in the world. Argentina's next Test after this is Canada at the World Cup in October 2027, plenty of time to enjoy beating a scrum-half at 10.

espn-604010.headline: Wales won five in 32. Australia look like the sixth
beats: Australia have lost three straight and conceded 50, 43 and 45 doing it, the last at Twickenham against England. Ryan Lonergan has since been defending Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii from the criticism that followed.
Wales beat Japan 28–21 on 7 November. That was only their fifth win in 32 Tests since the 2023 World Cup. In July, South Africa beat them 43–0.

Wales scored four tries against Japan. Australia have managed three in each of their last three defeats. Win, and Wales go up to ninth in the world, with Australia dropping to eighth, below Argentina.
Wales go to France in February. Australia's next Test is Hong Kong at the 2027 World Cup, which is a long time to sit on whatever happens in Cardiff.
